function.mechanism: Provides nitrate in curing systems, serving as a nitrite source that helps control microbial growth (including botulism risk) and supports cured-meat color/flavor characteristics.

adi.basis: Expressed as nitrate ion; EFSA communication on 2017 re-evaluation reported no need to change existing safe level.

efsa.key_finding: At permitted additive uses, nitrite/nitrate levels were considered sufficiently protective; additive-only nitrate exposure generally stayed within safe levels, while total dietary nitrate from all sources may exceed ADI in some groups.

adi.basis: Expressed as nitrate ion; JECFA retained this ADI in the 2002 nitrate entry and notes ADI does not apply to infants below 3 months in potassium nitrate record.

concerns.summary: IARC classifies ingested nitrate/nitrite under endogenous nitrosation conditions as Group 2A, and EFSA flags nitrosamine-formation pathways as a key concern context.

Recent prospective cohort evidence reported positive associations between higher potassium nitrate preservative intake and cancer incidence, but design is observational and residual confounding remains possible.

Animal and mechanistic studies using nitrate contexts (often sodium nitrate or co-exposure models) report endocrine/metabolic disruption signals, supporting biological plausibility but not direct human causal proof for E252 alone.
key_references: J Nutr Biochem 2025 zebrafish co-exposure study (PMID: 40023200)
Int J Hyg Environ Health 2026 scoping review (PMID: 41248583)

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA concluded nitrite/nitrate additives at permitted levels are sufficiently protective for consumers.
JECFA ADI framework for nitrate remains established at 0-3.7 mg/kg bw/day (as nitrate ion).

populations: children with high intake of foods containing nitrite/nitrate additives
medium/high total dietary nitrate consumers across age groups when all sources are included
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported additive-only nitrate exposure generally below ADI, but all-source dietary nitrate may exceed ADI in some population groups.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulators continue to authorize E252 with ADI/conditions, but exceedance scenarios, mechanistic nitrosation concerns, and emerging cohort associations argue against a low-concern tier.
key_factors: IARC Group 2A hazard context for nitrate/nitrite under endogenous nitrosation conditions
Exposure caveats for children and high total-dietary-exposure groups
Recent observational associations involving potassium nitrate preservative exposure
